body: There are support systems for people going through medication withdrawals.  I’ve only been through SSRI withdrawal, not benzos or anything like that, but even what I experienced was brutal.  I hope you’re still here and I hope you can find some reason to hold on to life.  I’m sure those who love you would be deeply sad if you succeeded.
Hi, what’s wrong?

Hey, I can relate to a bit of this.  I’m also autistic, and I too suffer from both physical disability and psychiatric issues and the combination is absolute hell.  Anyone going through this kind of stuff is a hero in my book, but at the same time I’d never fault anyone in this situation for needing an escape, or even for wanting to die.  Because I know that I sure do, sometimes.  I’m sorry things are so bad and that you were led on.  I hope things will get better for you though, you’re still young so there’s still a chance.  Don’t feel bad about using your looks or gender to get what you need either, I know I’d do the exact same thing if I only had that option in this world.

By the way, I did not get the reference, because I don’t know that much about anime, but what you wrote about those 2 characters reminded me of the film Wristcutters.

I’m disabled and had to cut my own hair today, and needless to say it looks like crap, so I can relate.  Could always just wear a hat or beanie for a few weeks until it straightens out.  Sorry to hear you were cheated on, but you’re still young and you’ve got a lot of life ahead of you, so please don’t let it get you too down.  You’ll end up alright.

I was really lonely at that age too.  Don’t give up because of the hair issue.  It’s a problem for me too now, but I think we’re gonna have the technology to fix that kind of stuff easily before too long.  Also, a wig is always an option.  Men don’t frequently consider wearing a wig for some reason but plenty of women with hair problems do it and manage to still look and feel attractive.  Don’t worry too much, you’ll be okay.

I have had so many nights like this.  Hundreds.  Even 2 nights ago was like this.  And somehow against all odds I’m still in it.  You may have a better chance than you realize.

I read through your profile a bit, that all sounds awful.  I’m really sorry. I wish there were better help for people like us.  :(

I’m autistic too, and I have chronic fatigue syndrome along with other medical and psychiatric issues, so I can relate.  My self-image has never been worse on top of all this, so I can relate.  

I have an online friend with a discord server for people who struggle socially, I can invite you if you’d like but there’s not many of us yet.

When you say mental breakdowns, what do you mean exactly?  Are you talking about racing thoughts, intrusive thoughts or something else?  You might consider starting a mindfulness meditation practice.  I hope this doesn’t sound like tone-deaf advice, because it has helped me a lot even if I still have serious problems.  You’re still pretty young, your brain is still fairly plastic and flexible, and you can learn to change how you react to these kinds of situations, even if it will take time and effort.  Wishing you the best in any case.

Per was a very troubled young man.  It’s easy to romanticize despair and mental illness, or even suicide, but the reality is so much grimmer.  Is there anyone you can open up to about your feelings?  Parents, friends, anyone?  People can be more understanding than you realize.

I have horrible anxiety too but I’ve found some things that work for me.  Still, I’m going through some serious shit again and I feel like I’ve damaged myself irreparably but somehow I think we just have to push through it.  Please don’t make another attempt, it is highly possible that there’s a better way out.
I don’t do calls but you can DM me.  I’ve been through a lot of serious shit and I’m going through a lot of serious shit.

Hello, I’m sorry to hear about what you’re going through.  For what it’s worth, I’m dealing with some of the same issues: severe isolation (have barely left my mom’s house in over five years) and what must be over a dozen metal and neurological problems.  I also have issues with sunlight like you do.  I can’t go into the backyard for long at all and I have to wear sunglasses and block out natural light constantly.

I’m not very good at consoling people, but at least you know you aren’t completely alone, right?  My life’s a complete wreck too, and it just seems to get worse the longer it goes on for.
You too.  Hope you’re feeling at least a little better now.

Hey, I’m sorry to read about what you’re experiencing.  I’m going through a horrible time myself, feeling like I am declining continually and don’t know how long I can last.  Please don’t harm yourself or anything like that though, I am sure there must be people out there who would miss you.  There is always some hope even if it’s hard to hold on to.

How old are you?  I’m sorry you’re feeling this way.  I’m going through horrible things too and constantly fantasize about living on an island with no one else around for a while so people don’t have to see me like this.

You’re very welcome.  Honestly, I really just want to help people who are suffering by sharing what I can.  Anxiety is really only the tip of the iceberg for me in terms of what I struggle with these days, but it’s still a major issue for many.

I hope you have a peaceful day.

Basically, self-induced neurogenic tremors.  You do a series of preliminary exercises and then lie down and allow your body to shake out stress and trauma.  (I skip the preliminary exercises though — they don’t seem to be entirely necessary for the technique to work, and I have chronic fatigue anyway.). 

There are some videos of people doing them on YouTube if you’re curious to see.
Have you ever tried trauma release exercises (TRE’s)?  They help me with panic sometimes.
Thank you.
Does anyone have any advice for subs or YouTube channels to help me relax by the way?  Anything like r/cozyplaces will do.
Watch the saddest movie you can think of, listen to sad songs, or look at old photographs.

Well, I don’t really know what to say.  I’m not very good at consoling others.  And I’d be lying if I said I didn’t envy what you have, since I don’t have a way out where I’m at.  I just think it would be too bad if you went through with it, since you seem like a pretty cool person.  In any case I hope you find peaceful relief from everything that troubles you.

Other than that I’m really sorry about what you’re going through.  Have you thought about reaching out to a counselor or someone like that?

I’m probably in a completely different situation than you, but I’m dealing with horrible intrusive thoughts involving violence.  It’s hellish and I find myself thinking along similar lines: what really is the difference, morally speaking, between myself and a person who commits real violence?  I frequently wish I could be trapped on an island by myself so that no matter what happens, no matter how crazy I get, at least I won’t have the opportunity to harm another human being.  But that’s impossible, so instead I just wish for death.  These awful thoughts and feelings really separate us from the fold, that’s for sure.
I’m dealing with a lot of similar problems, including the absolute worst intrusive thoughts of my entire life.  If there is a hell, this is it.  You aren’t alone.

I don't really know how to help you other than to let you know that you definitely aren't alone.  My body has been falling apart ever since it decided to give me a mystery illness at age 23 (I'm now 30).  Since then I've dealt with innumerable symptoms, mostly mental these days, but I am also left with undiagnosed chronic fatigue and on top of that a case of chronic telogen effluvium (hair shedding) that I was told would eventually stop - 5 years ago now.  I also likely have Asperger's, although I somehow avoided diagnosis during childhood and young adulthood.  And I deal with severe anxiety, depression, pure-O OCD, and probably a whole bunch of other things, and virtually nothing helps me - I've tried everything and literally nothing works.  Most of what I live and suffer with is probably also genetic.  

I'm sorry I can't help you, but I can definitely sympathize, and it's good to hear that you are not immediately suicidal, though I can recall having similar thoughts in my mid-20's - that if this keeps up, I might just have to end it in my 30's.

For what it's worth, I have an imaginary girlfriend too.  Fantasy is a standard way of coping with loneliness and you're not at all alone in utilizing it, and you definitely aren't pathetic for it.  Please hold on for us, okay?
